title: Anticipatory KPI Hedge and Launch Canvas
content:
Executive summary:

This is a working canvas to track the next product launch (internal codename: Orion) with an explicit KPI hedge: defined guardrail thresholds, pre-authorized mitigation levers, and owner-level commitments for the first 72h after go-live. Goal is to turn ambiguity about acceptable deviation into bounded actions so on-call + product ops can act without waiting for a full incident postmortem.

Why this doc exists (context):
- Product: new traffic-tiered rollout for model routing and tiered pricing (hosted API + dedicated pool burst).
- Problem: small changes in batching/cache heuristics combined with a traffic shift may increase p99 latency or per-token cost beyond commercial thresholds.
- Outcome desired: deterministic decision surface for slow degradations (latency/cost/quality).

Top-level KPIs and hedge bands (owner, target, warning, trigger, hard-stop):
- API p99 latency (global): owner: SRE-Traffic, target: <= 180ms, warning: 180-260ms, trigger: >260ms (investigate + throttle), hard-stop: >400ms (rollback canary).
- Median token cost (USD/1k tokens): owner: Finance-IO, target: <= $0.32, warning: $0.32-$0.40, trigger: >$0.40 (activate cost-mode routing), hard-stop: >$0.60 (pause heavy features).
- Error rate (5xx per minute): owner: Serving-Runtime, target: <0.05%, warning: 0.05%-0.2%, trigger: >0.2% (limit new sessions), hard-stop: >1% (rollback).
- Model-quality regression (eval prompt set): owner: Applied-ML, target: delta <= 0.5% relative to baseline, warning: 0.5%-1.5%, trigger: >1.5% (failover to previous variant), hard-stop: >3% (halt rollout).
- Adoption (new route adoption % of traffic): owner: Product-Analytics, target: 5% weekly, warning: 2-5%, trigger: <2% (pause marketing), hard-stop: N/A.

Pre-authorized mitigation levers (what to do at each trigger band):
- Warning band (investigate fast, prepare):
  - Flip on higher-priority prefix caching for recent prefixes (runtime toggle).
  - Reduce max batch size by 10% on Canary (serving flag).
  - Notify ops and product slack channel (#orion-launch).
  - Increase telemetry sampling for traces and prompts.
- Trigger band (automated actions + human review):
  - Route a percentage (configurable) of requests to fallback model variant with quantized profile (cost/latency tradeoff).
  - Enforce per-tenant rate-limits for non-critical routes.
  - Engage Solutions Eng to give immediate customer-facing notes for enterprise beta.
- Hard-stop (immediate safety actions):
  - Abort rollout (traffic back to baseline routing).
  - Roll back the config changes introduced in the canary.
  - If cost runaway: isolate and freeze high-cost tenants.

Decision matrix (quick lookup):
- If p99 >260ms and 5xx >0.2% -> reduce canary traffic by 50% + enable fallback route.
- If cost per 1k tokens >$0.40 and adoption <2% -> pause billing changes and throttle heavy endpoints.
- If model quality delta >1.5% -> immediate rollback of model variant for affected region.
- If multiple triggers fire across categories -> declare "Tier-2 Launch Incident" and engage full oncall war room.

Owner RACI and contact quicklist:
- Product ops lead (R): Samira Kaur (samira@redwood.ai)
- Serving runtime (A): Omar Ruiz (omar@redwood.ai)
- SRE-Traffic (C): Ethan Park (ethan@redwood.ai)
- Applied-ML (C): Marta Li (marta@redwood.ai)
- Finance-IO (I): Lina Morales (lina@redwood.ai)
- Escalation path: product-ops -> eng-manager -> head of infra (if >60 min unresolved on trigger).

Roadmap tracker (30/60/90 slice, owners, acceptance):
- 0-30d (pre-launch prep):
  - Canary config baked (owner: Serving-Runtime). Acceptance: canary traffic toggle, smoke tests pass (SLO smoke: p95 < 150ms).
  - KPI dashboards assembled (owner: Product-Analytics). Acceptance: realtime p99, cost-per-token, model-eval delta panels.
  - Cost hedges defined in billing service (owner: Finance-IO). Acceptance: automatic routing to cost-mode when threshold hit.
- 31-60d (soft launch):
  - Beta customers (3 partners) onboarded to dedicated pool. Acceptance: dedicated pool sustain 2k rps for 1h.
  - Surge runbook validated with SRE playbook drill. Acceptance: <5% deviation from modeled p99 in 2 of 3 drills.
- 61-90d (open rollout):
  - Full feature flag rollout to 20% traffic. Acceptance: no triggers across KPIs for 7 consecutive days.

Launch readiness checklist (preflight quickchecks):
- Telemetry: Trace sampling at 10x baseline enabled; custom span for model_lookup and kernel_selector present.
- Observability: alerting thresholds configured in prometheus/opsgenie with escalation chain.
- Testing: end-to-end smoke tests with golden prompts run daily and pass >=95% on Canary.
- Capacity: Dedicated pools have 15% headroom at evaluated seq_len=2048 distribution.
- Security/compliance: KMS policy for customer-managed keys validated for private deployments.
- Billing: Billing quota grace configured for first-week surge.
- Docs: Customer-facing short-notes + internal runbook updated (links in linked_artifacts).

Go/No-Go quick rubric (30-minute decision cadence before traffic ramps):
- Green: all critical KPIs in target band for 72h on canary, no open blockers, runbook annotated. -> Proceed.
- Yellow: up to one warning-band violation; owners have mitigation plan and pre-authorized toggles. -> Proceed with caution (slow ramp, 2x monitoring cadence).
- Red: any hard-stop metric breached or two trigger-band violations across categories in 60min. -> Abort and rollback.

Simulated surge notes (bench results & takeaways):
- Scenario: 2x baseline traffic for 45 minutes with heavy long-context prompts (90th percentile seq_len ~ 1800).
  - Observed: p99 increased to 320ms on hosted-routed requests; dedicated pool p99 stayed <200ms.
  - Actionable: ensure routing policy favors dedicated pool for long-context prompts; add prefix detection to route early.
  - Simulation gap: billing metrics had 15m ingestion lag — need faster ingestion to hit cost trigger in time.

Open questions and follow-ups (action items):
- (A1) Shorten billing metric ingestion window to <=5m. Owner: Finance-IO. Due: 2026-03-01.
- (A2) Add automated prefix hot-caching toggle and test under juggle load. Owner: Serving-Runtime. Due: 2026-03-05.
- (A3) Define exact percent split for fallback routing (suggested default 30%). Owner: Product-Analytics + SRE-Traffic. Due: 2026-02-20.
- (A4) Customer comms template for pauses (legal/CS review). Owner: Customer-Success. Due: 2026-02-18.

Lightweight runbook snippets (copy to incident channel):
- "If p99 >260ms for 10m: reduce canary traffic by 50% via rollout toggle and post status with simple template: 'Orion canary: p99 breach -> traffic at 50%'"
- "If cost >$0.40/1k tokens for 15m: enable cost-mode routing, notify finance, open ticket JIRA-PRJ-1123-COST"

Notes to self / informal bits (brainstorming fragments):
- We should consider a temporary price floor test so enterprise partners aren’t surprised by short-term per-token spikes.
- Can we synthesize a small set of golden prompts that exercise kernel selection to catch regressions faster? (talk to Applied-ML).
- Might be worth a "traffic olympics" monthly where product-ops, SRE, serving runtime run one simulated blast with different kernel/quantization combos.

Appendix (quick links):
- Canary smoke dashboard: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/sku-orion-canary
- Playbook draft confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/launch-playbook-2026
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-sim/pull/58

Last notes: This is intentionally prescriptive and minimal: capture a small decision surface and a tight set of mitigations so folks can act quickly without full context. Update this doc after each drill with observed reaction times and the lead-time needed to hit each mitigation.
summary: Working canvas to track Orion launch with KPI hedge bands, mitigation levers, owners, and a go/no-go rubric for 72h post-launch.
